hints: Look closely at the word saturated in saturated fatty acid. What does that tell you about C=C double bonds in its hydrocarbon tail?
Remember that every peptide bond in a protein contains a C=O, and the haem group in haemoglobin has a ring full of conjugated double bonds. How many of those would a large protein have?
walkthrough:
**Check the saturated fatty acid first**

Saturated means no C=C double bonds between carbons in the tail. It is full of single bonds with hydrogen.

The only double bond is the one C=O in its single carboxyl (-COOH) group, so it has just 1 double bond, not at least 3.

**Check the two proteins, collagen and haemoglobin**

Both are very large polypeptides made of hundreds of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

Each peptide bond contains a C=O double bond, so any large protein automatically contains hundreds of double bonds.

**Give haemoglobin an extra check**

Haemoglobin also contains four haem groups. Each haem has a porphyrin ring with many alternating C=C and C=N double bonds.

So both collagen and haemoglobin easily have far more than three double bonds, while saturated fatty acid does not. That points to C.

options.A: Incorrect because saturated fatty acid has only one double bond (the C=O in COOH), so it cannot be included.
options.B: Incorrect because although collagen qualifies, saturated fatty acid does not have at least three double bonds.
options.C: Correct because both are proteins with hundreds of C=O bonds in peptide bonds, and haemoglobin has extra double bonds in its four haem rings.
options.D: Incorrect because although haemoglobin qualifies, saturated fatty acid has only one double bond and so fails the test.
